blurb: Slender, blue-eyed colourpoint cat from Thailand, one of the oldest recognised breeds
description: The Siamese is a slender cat breed from Thailand with a short, glossy colourpoint coat, blue almond-shaped eyes and a social, affectionate, outgoing nature.
answer: The Siamese is one of the first distinctly recognised cat breeds, developed from the Wichianmat landrace of Thailand, once called Siam. It has a short, glossy colourpoint coat, blue almond-shaped eyes and a long, slender body. It is commonly described as affectionate, intelligent and very social.

body: Colourpointed Wichianmat cats are described in the Tamra Maew, Thai cat-book poems thought to date from the Ayutthaya Kingdom. In 1878 US President Rutherford B. Hayes received the first documented Siamese in the United States, and in 1884 British Consul-General Edward Gould brought a breeding pair to Britain. From the 1950s breeders favoured an increasingly slender, angular type, and from the 1980s the traditional rounder cats were split off as a separate breed, the Thai.

The modern Siamese has a long, tubular, muscular body, a triangular head, large wide-set ears, light blue almond-shaped eyes and a slender tail. The short, fine coat has no undercoat. Its points come from a heat-sensitive form of albinism, so the cooler extremities are darker and cats tend to darken with age. Kittens are born cream to white. Point colours include seal, blue, chocolate, lilac, red and cream, with tabby and tortie patterns.

Siamese are usually described as very affectionate, intelligent and social, sometimes called extroverts, and many bond strongly with one person. One author describes them as more likely than other cats to stay close to their owner and less likely to hunt.
Sources give little specific detail on care. The short, close-lying coat is generally low-maintenance, and as a social breed it is usually said to enjoy company and interaction.

A UK study found a life expectancy of 11.69 years, close to the average for all cats. Conditions reported in the breed include mammary tumours, gastrointestinal problems, progressive retinal atrophy, gangliosidosis and some forms of hair loss. The colourpoint gene also affects eye-brain wiring, which once made many Siamese cross-eyed.

faq.q: Why do Siamese cats have dark points?
faq.a: Their colourpoint pattern comes from a heat-sensitive enzyme that produces pigment only in cooler parts of the body, such as the ears, face, paws and tail.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Siamese and a Thai cat?
faq.a: Both descend from the Wichianmat, but the Thai keeps the traditional rounder build, while the modern Siamese is bred slender and angular.

faq.q: How long do Siamese cats live?
faq.a: A UK study found a life expectancy of 11.69 years, close to the average for all cats.
